gist: Opens the chapter giving 'The Six Keys of Eudoxus' and covers the First, Second and Third Keys: the first purification of the Stone to whiteness, its philosophic sublimation and dissolution by the Secret Fire, and the long preparation of 'our Mercury' by dissolving the body, washing the earth with its own water to extract the Fixed Salt, and reuniting soul, spirit and body. The whole is in the first-person voice of the Keys' author as named in the chapter heading; the chunk breaks off mid-discussion of the water's names.

notes.point: Heading: 'The Six Keys of Eudoxus'. Text is first-person ('I will enlarge myself'); no Atwood comment in this chunk.
First Key opens the dark prisons of the Sulphur, extracts the seed from the body, forms the Stone by conjoining spirit with body (sulphur with mercury).
Hermes: the Stone hidden in the caverns of the metals, bright, 'a mind sublime', the Sea of the Wise where they angle for their Fish.
The three works are analogous and philosophers speak equivocally so those without 'Lynx's eyes' confuse one work for another.

Each work: dissolve body with spirit, cut off Raven's head, whiten Black, vivify White; but cutting off the Black Dragon's and Raven's head belongs properly to the First operation. Hermes: what is born of the Crow begins the Art.
Separating the black, stinking fume of the Blackest Black forms the white Stone holding 'the blood of the Pelican'; First Key ends at this first purification and whiteness.
Second Key dissolves the Stone's compound and separates the Elements by raising subtle and pure above thick and earthy (sublimation).

Only the Fire of the Wise can sublime; it is never openly revealed. Who cannot recognize it should stop and pray: it is a gift of Heaven more than reasoning; yet read, meditate, pray (Work, Meditation, Prayer).
Sublimation enables conversion of Elements (Earth to Water, Water to Air, Air to Fire), the only way to prepare our Mercury.

The Secret Fire dissolves the Stone gently into Water in the sea of the Wise by distillation 'made by the rays of the Sun and Moon'; the Stone (Hermes' vine) becomes Wine, yielding Water of Life and sharp Vinegar.
Only 'this Nature wholly Divine' dissolves the Elements; perfect dissolution follows proportioned digestion and putrefaction, ending the Second Key 'of the First Work'.
Third Key: longer than all others together; philosophers, even Artefius, Trevisan, Flammel, keep silent or feign on the Preparation of Mercury. Author promises to set it in order.
Its aim: separate and purify Mercury's Principles by dissolving and glorifying the body it came from and uniting soul with body, Spirit the only tie; ends in a far nobler new substance.

The water/wine from the Stone hides three principles, Salt, Sulphur, Mercury (spirit, soul, body), not truly united: distilling off the Water (soul and spirit) leaves the Body as dead black earth, not to be despised.
Pontanus: even the Stone's superfluities become essence; nothing may be separated from the subject; 'our Fire' perfects the whole. Against keeping only the subtle.

Hermes: power not integral until turned into earth. Fire and Sulphur lie in the Earth's centre; wash the earth with its spirit to extract the Fixed Salt, Blood of our Stone, by gentle digestion and slow distillation.
Reconcile fire and water, enemies who radically love each other; Cosmopolite: purged, they become friends in their earth. Moisten the earth often with its water.
Body must be dissolved and earth penetrated with humidity for generation: Spirit is Eve, Body Adam. Hermes: Water excites the fixed Nature in the Body.
United, they rise together leaving little faeces; soul, spirit, body form a nobler Form, as rectified spirit of wine 'actuated with its salt' differs from wine.
Our Water springs from the Stone, the Art's foundation (Hermes); called wine, water of life, vinegar, oil by degree or effect; properly Vinegar of the Wise.

As with vinegar, water and phlegm rise first, the efficacious oily part last; so dissolve the body wholly to extract all humidity with its sulphur-ferment, without which the desired blackness never appears.

Reduce the whole to water, uniting volatile and fixed; Senior: highest fume to lowest; the divine water returns soul to body and revives it. Wash the faeces, where the Balm of Life hides, until no longer black; the Water then holds the Fiery Essence.
Two compounds: of Nature (First Key), made by Nature with the Artist only assisting; of Art, made by the Artist uniting fixed and volatile, differing somewhat in Second and Third Work.
Geber: Argent vive and Sulphur, volatile and fixed, fix each other perfectly; as earth needs moisture and moisture needs earth's dryness.

First work: purify the Serpent of the earth's slime, whiten the black faeces to separate the white sulphur (Sal Amoniac, Chaste Diana); the mystery is extracting the fixed salt, all of Mercury's energy.
Distilled water carries up fiery salt; repeated affusion fertilizes the Mercury until fit to be fixed, 'the end of the second Work'. Hermes rejoiced as the water thickened.
The viscous liquor is Pontick Water, its ponticity the mark of virtue, growing with rectification; Water of Life as giving life to metals; properly great Lunaria for its brightness. Breaks off.

method.veiled: the dark prisons in which the Sulphur is shut up
method.plain: The body that encloses the active principle (Sulphur/seed); the First Key frees it.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3: the same sentence glosses the First Key as that which 'knows how to extract the seed out of the body'.

method.veiled: extract the seed out of the body
method.plain: Draw the generative principle out of the material body; this is the First Key's task.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3 gives this as what the First Key does.

method.veiled: conjunction of the spirit with the body -- of sulphur with mercury
method.plain: The Stone is formed by joining spirit and body; 'sulphur with mercury' is given as another name for the same joining.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3 sets the two pairs in apposition.

method.veiled: In the caverns of the metals there is hidden the Stone
method.plain: The Stone lies concealed inside metallic bodies and has to be uncovered (First Key).
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3 cites it as Hermes' demonstration of the First Key, which opens prisons and extracts seed from body.

method.veiled: it is the Sea of the Wise, in which they angle for their mysterious Fish
method.plain: The Stone is itself the medium out of which the sages draw something hidden; the text does not say what the Fish is.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3 calls the Stone 'an open sea' and 'the Sea of the Wise'; the Fish is left unexplained.

method.veiled: those who have not the Lynx's eyes may pursue wrong
method.plain: The operator needs sharp discernment to tell which of three analogous works a writer means, because the philosophers speak equivocally on purpose.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3: equivocal terms are used so that those without Lynx's eyes go wrong; 'when one imagines that they speak of one work, they often treat of another'.

method.veiled: the Wise Artist ought to dissolve the body with the spirit
method.plain: In every work the body is dissolved by means of the spirit.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3, said to hold 'in each work'.

method.veiled: he must cut off the Raven's head, whiten the Black, and vivify the White
method.plain: A recurring three-step sequence in each work: remove the black stage, bring it to white, then give life to the white.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3: the black, foul fume is separated so the white Stone forms; the First Key ends 'at this shining whiteness'.

method.veiled: it is properly in the First operation that the Wise Artist cuts off the head of the Black Dragon and of the Raven
method.plain: The removal of the black matter belongs chiefly to the first operation.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3 follows it with the separation of 'the black, foul, and stinking fume of the Blackest Black' that forms the white Stone.

method.veiled: What is born of the Crow is the beginning of this Art.
method.plain: The Art begins from what comes out of the black stage.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3 introduces it with 'Hence' after the Raven/Black Dragon passage.

method.veiled: by separation of the black, foul, and stinking fume of the Blackest Black that our astral, white, and resplendent Stone is formed
method.plain: The white Stone results from separating out a dark, foul vapour.

method.veiled: at this First Purification of the Stone, and at this shining whiteness, that the work of the First Key is ended
method.plain: Shining whiteness marks the end of the First Key.

method.veiled: which contains in its veins the blood of the Pelican
method.plain: The white Stone holds an inner vital substance; the text does not say what 'blood of the Pelican' is (see ambiguities).
method.basis: IV.3 ¶3 only; compare 'the Fixed Salt, which is the Blood of our Stone' in IV.3 ¶7.

method.veiled: raising up the subtle and pure parts above the thick and terrestrial parts
method.plain: Philosophic separation of the Elements means raising the fine, pure part above the coarse, earthy part, i.e. sublimation.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5 defines the separation this way and then calls it sublimation.

method.veiled: the Fire of the Wise, which is the only instrument which can work this sublimation
method.plain: A special 'fire', never openly named, is the sole agent of the sublimation; the text gives its functions (dissolves the Stone naturally, without violence, into water) but not its identity.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5: 'No philosopher has ever openly revealed this Secret Fire'; it 'dissolves the Stone naturally and without violence'.

method.veiled: the knowledge of this great Secret is rather a gift of Heaven, than a Light acquired by the natural force of reasoning
method.plain: Knowing the Secret Fire depends more on illumination than on reasoning; the seeker should read the philosophers, meditate and pray.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5: 'there is no difficulty which may not in the end be made clear by Work, Meditation, and Prayer'.

method.veiled: this conversion, which makes Water of Earth, Air of Water, and Fire of Air
method.plain: A stepwise conversion of the Elements, each into the next finer one, which follows on sublimation and is the only way to prepare 'our Mercury'.

method.veiled: makes it dissolve into Water in the great sea of the Wise, by the distillation which is made by the rays of the Sun and Moon
method.plain: The Secret Fire dissolves the Stone into a water through a distillation the text ascribes to 'the rays of the Sun and Moon'; whether literal or figurative is not stated.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5 only; see ambiguities.

method.veiled: the Stone, which, according to Hermes, is the vine of the Wise, becomes their Wine
method.plain: Once dissolved, the Stone is called 'Wine'; from it Art derives 'rectified Water of Life' and 'most sharp Vinegar'.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5: 'It is in this manner' refers back to the dissolution into Water.

method.veiled: this Nature wholly Divine
method.plain: The only thing that can dissolve the Stone's Elements; in context, the Secret Fire.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5: the Secret Fire 'dissolves the Stone', and a few lines later the Elements 'cannot be dissolved but by this Nature wholly Divine'.

method.veiled: a proportioned digestion and putrefaction, at which the operation of the Second Key of the First Work is ended
method.plain: Perfect dissolution needs measured digestion and putrefaction, which close the Second Key.

method.veiled: the Preparation of our Mercury
method.plain: The longest and most important operation, belonging to the Third Key, which the philosophers have passed over or feigned about.

method.veiled: a perfect dissolution and glorification of the body, whence it had its nativity
method.plain: The Principles of Mercury are separated and purified by fully dissolving and exalting the body they came from.

method.veiled: the intimate union of the soul with its body, of whom the Spirit is the only tie which works this conjunction
method.plain: Soul and body are reunited only through the spirit as intermediary.

method.veiled: the generation of a new substance infinitely nobler than the First
method.plain: The Third Key ends in a new, far nobler substance.

method.veiled: made a spring of living water come out of the stone, and has pressed out the vine of the philosophers, and has made their wine
method.plain: Starting point of the Third Key: the Stone has already been dissolved into its water/'wine' (the Second Key's result).
method.basis: IV.3 ¶5 describes the Stone ('vine of the Wise') becoming 'their Wine' by dissolution; IV.3 ¶7 opens 'After' these steps.

method.veiled: three natural principles of bodies --- Salt, Sulphur and Mercury --- which are the spirit, the soul, and the body
method.plain: The apparently uniform water contains three distinct principles, still not truly united, that must be separated and purified.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7; the one-to-one pairing is ambiguous (see ambiguities).

method.veiled: the Body remains in the bottom of the vessel, like a dead, black, and dredgy earth
method.plain: When the water (soul and spirit) is distilled off, a dark residue (the body) remains; it must be kept, not discarded.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'which, nevertheless, is not to be despised'.

method.veiled: persuade themselves that they must only take the subtile and cast away the heavy
method.plain: Error: treating purification as keeping the fine part and discarding the residue. The whole compound, dregs included, must be perfected.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7, following Pontanus: 'he who pretends to separate anything from our subject knows nothing of philosophy'.

method.veiled: power of it is not integral until it be turned into earth
method.plain: The matter reaches full power only once it is fixed into an earthy, solid state.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: given against discarding the heavy part, followed by the Fire and Sulphur being hidden 'in the centre of the Earth'.

method.veiled: they must wash it exactly with its spirit, to extract out of it the Fixed Salt, which is the Blood of our Stone
method.plain: Repeatedly wash the residual earth with the distilled spirit drawn from it, to draw out its fixed salt; done with gentle digestion and slow distillation.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'not accomplished till after a convenient digestion and a slow distillation'.

method.veiled: the Wise Artist must make peace between the enemies, who radically love each other vehemently
method.plain: Reconcile the contraries fire and water so they unite; this happens in their own earth once purged.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7, with the Cosmopolite citation.

method.veiled: moisten oftentimes the earth with its water, and you will obtain what you seek
method.plain: Repeatedly re-wet the residual earth with the water distilled from it.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7; compare IV.3 ¶9 'affusion of the water on the body, reiterated many times'.

method.veiled: the Spirit is Eve, the Body is Adam; they ought to be joined together for the propagation of their species
method.plain: Spirit and body are a female and male pair that must be united for generation.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7: 'these two substances, which are of the same nature but of different genders'.

method.veiled: ascend insensibly together, leaving but a little faeces in the bottom of their vessel
method.plain: When united, spirit and body rise together, leaving little residue; this signals their union.

method.veiled: as the alcohol of Wine exactly rectified and actuated with its salt is different from the substance of the wine
method.plain: The reunited soul, spirit and body are to the first liquid what rectified spirit of wine charged with its own salt is to plain wine.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶7 calls the comparison 'very fitting' and a 'precise knowledge of the operations of the Third Key'.

method.veiled: Our Water is a living Spring which comes out of the Stone by a natural miracle
method.plain: The water drawn from the Stone is the foundation of the Art; it is properly called the Vinegar of the Wise.

method.veiled: the water and the phlegm ascend first; the oily substance, in which the efficacy of the water consists, comes the last
method.plain: In distilling, the watery part rises first and the potent oily part last, so the body must be fully dissolved to get all of it.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶8: 'It is therefore necessary to dissolve the body entirely'.

method.veiled: the precious ferment, the sulphur, that balm of Nature, and wonderful unguent
method.plain: The humidity of the body holds the active sulphur; without extracting it the desired blackness will not appear.

method.veiled: this blackness so desired by all the philosophers
method.plain: A blackness in the vessel is a desired sign, which appears only if the body's humidity is fully extracted.

method.veiled: the highest fume should be reduced to the lowest
method.plain: What has risen as vapour must be brought back down onto the residue, uniting volatile with fixed.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶8: given with 'make a perfect union of the volatile with the fixed' and the water as 'reducer of the soul to its body'.

method.veiled: the divine water is the thing descending from heaven, the reducer of the soul to its body, which it at length revives
method.plain: The water, returned onto the body, carries the soul back to it and revives it.

method.veiled: you ought to wash them with this celestial water until you have removed away the blackness from them
method.plain: Wash the dark residue with the water until it is no longer black; then the water becomes charged with the 'Fiery Essence'.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶8: 'The Balm of Life is hid in these unclean faeces'.

method.veiled: who does nothing but lend a hand to Nature by the adhibition of external things
method.plain: For the compound of Nature (First Key) the Artist only assists Nature by applying outside means; Nature produces it.

method.veiled: the secret union of the fixed with the volatile, perfectly conjoined with all prudence
method.plain: The compound of Art is made by the Artist by uniting fixed and volatile, which requires profound philosophy.

method.veiled: volatilized and fixed reciprocally into a perfect Fixity
method.plain: Volatile and fixed act on each other until the whole becomes fixed; illustrated by earth needing moisture and moisture needing earth's dryness.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9, Geber's definition and the example of Nature.

method.veiled: purify the Serpent, born of the Slime of the earth
method.plain: A first-work task, paired with whitening the black faeces; what the Serpent denotes is not stated.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9 only.

method.veiled: the white sulphur, which is the Sal Amoniac of the Wise, and their Chaste Diana, who washes herself in the bath
method.plain: Whitening the black faeces separates a white sulphur; the 'mystery' is the extraction of the fixed salt of the compound.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9: 'all this mystery is but the extraction of the fixed salt of our compound'.

method.veiled: the affusion of the water on the body, reiterated many times, impregnates, fattens, and fertilizes our Mercury
method.plain: Distilled water carries up part of the fiery salt; pouring it back on the body many times enriches the Mercury until it can be fixed.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9: 'which is the end of the second Work'.

method.veiled: the water by degrees did become thicker and harder
method.plain: Progressive thickening of the water shows the work is succeeding.
method.basis: IV.3 ¶9: 'I certainly knew that I should find what I sought for'.

method.veiled: Its exuberant ponticity is indeed the true character of its virtue
method.plain: The viscous liquor's ponticity marks its strength, which increases with rectification and working.

terms.meaning: One of six successive stages of the operation set out in this chapter. First Key: freeing the seed/Sulphur and forming the white Stone. Second Key: sublimation and dissolution of the Stone. Third Key: the preparation of our Mercury.

quotes.text: The Third Key comprehends of itself alone a longer train of operations than all the rest together.

terms.meaning: Three analogous works whose operations resemble one another, which the philosophers deliberately confuse. How they map onto the Keys is not fully clear (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: the operations of the three works have a great deal of analogy one to another

terms.meaning: Formed in the First Key by joining spirit and body and by separating off the black fume; dissolved and sublimed in the Second Key; the source from which 'our Water' springs.

equivalences.quote: the Stone, which, according to Hermes, is the vine of the Wise
it is the Sea of the Wise, in which they angle for their mysterious Fish

quotes.text: forms the Stone of the philosophers by the conjunction of the spirit with the body

terms.meaning: Shut up in dark prisons and freed by the First Key; paired with mercury as spirit with body; one of the three principles; contained in the body's humidity as the precious ferment; hidden with the Fire in the centre of the Earth. The white sulphur is separated by whitening the black faeces.

equivalences.with: precious ferment / balm of Nature / wonderful unguent
equivalences.quote: the precious ferment, the sulphur, that balm of Nature, and wonderful unguent

equivalences.with: Sal Amoniac of the Wise / Chaste Diana
equivalences.quote: the white sulphur, which is the Sal Amoniac of the Wise, and their Chaste Diana

quotes.text: opens the dark prisons in which the Sulphur is shut up

terms.meaning: What the Third Key prepares; prepared only through conversion of the Elements; its Principles are separated and purified; its whole energy lies in the fixed salt; impregnated by repeated affusion until fit to be fixed.

quotes.text: the only way whereby our Mercury can be prepared
the extraction of the fixed salt of our compound, in which the whole energy of our Mercury consists

terms.meaning: The unrevealed agent of the Art, the only instrument of sublimation; dissolves the Stone naturally and without violence into water; perfects the whole compound, dregs included. Its identity is not given.

equivalences.quote: the Fire of the Wise, which is the only instrument which can work this sublimation. No philosopher has ever openly revealed this Secret Fire

quotes.text: this Secret Fire, which dissolves the Stone naturally and without violence

terms.meaning: Raising the subtle and pure parts above the thick and terrestrial; effected only by the Fire of the Wise; prerequisite for converting Elements and extracting Principles.

quotes.text: this separation of the elements is not made but by raising up the subtle and pure parts above the thick and terrestrial parts

terms.meaning: Separated philosophically in the Second Key and converted in sequence: Earth to Water, Water to Air, Air to Fire.

quotes.text: this conversion, which makes Water of Earth, Air of Water, and Fire of Air

terms.meaning: Three principles in the dissolved water: Salt, Sulphur and Mercury, also called spirit, soul and body. They seem united but must be separated, purified and reunited.

equivalences.quote: Salt, Sulphur and Mercury --- which are the spirit, the soul, and the body

quotes.text: though they appear pure and perfectly united together, there still wants much of their being so

terms.meaning: Three components of the matter. The distilled Water is soul and spirit; the body is the residue. Spirit is the only tie uniting soul with body. Spirit and Body are female and male (Eve and Adam), of the same nature but different genders.

equivalences.quote: the Water, which is the soul and the spirit
the Spirit is Eve, the Body is Adam

quotes.text: of whom the Spirit is the only tie which works this conjunction

terms.meaning: Extracted from the residual earth by washing it with its own spirit; called the Blood of our Stone; holds all the energy of our Mercury; partly carried up by the distilled water.

equivalences.quote: the Fixed Salt, which is the Blood of our Stone

quotes.text: a part of this fiery salt

terms.meaning: The water springing from the Stone, the foundation of the Art. Its names vary with degree of preparation or effect; properly the Vinegar of the Wise. Returned onto the body it reunites soul and body; animated by the Fiery Essence; when viscous it is called Pontick Water, Water of Life (giving life to metals), and properly the great Lunaria for its brightness.

equivalences.quote: it is properly called the Vinegar of the Wise

equivalences.with: wine, water of life, vinegar, oil
equivalences.quote: sometimes they call it wine, sometimes water of life, sometimes vinegar, sometimes oil
the philosophers give this viscous Liquor the name of Pontick Water
it is properly called the great Lunaria, because of its brightness

quotes.text: Our Water is a living Spring which comes out of the Stone by a natural miracle of our philosophy.

terms.meaning: A quality of the viscous water that is the true mark of its virtue and grows with rectification and working. The text gives no further definition.

quotes.text: Its exuberant ponticity is indeed the true character of its virtue

terms.meaning: Name for the Stone (Hermes) and the place where the Stone is dissolved into Water.

equivalences.quote: This Stone has a bright glittering: it contains a Spirit of a sublime original; it is the Sea of the Wise

quotes.text: makes it dissolve into Water in the great sea of the Wise

terms.term: Raven / Black Dragon / Crow / Blackest Black
terms.meaning: Images for the black stage or matter whose 'head' is cut off, mainly in the first operation, by separating the black, foul fume, from which the white Stone results.

quotes.text: he must cut off the Raven's head, whiten the Black, and vivify the White

variants: this blackness so desired by all the philosophers
terms.meaning: A desired appearance in the vessel, seen only if all the body's humidity (with its sulphur) is extracted; separately, the blackness of the faeces must be washed away.

quotes.text: without which you ought not to hope ever to see in your vessel this blackness so desired by all the philosophers

terms.meaning: The dark residue left after distilling off the water. It is not to be discarded: the Balm of Life is hidden in it, and it is washed and whitened to extract the fixed salt or white sulphur.

equivalences.quote: the Body remains in the bottom of the vessel, like a dead, black, and dredgy earth

quotes.text: The Balm of Life is hid in these unclean faeces

terms.meaning: Two kinds. The compound of Nature (First Key) is made by Nature with the Artist only assisting. The compound of Art is made by the Artist by secretly uniting fixed with volatile, and differs somewhat between the Second and Third Work. Per Geber, a mixture of Argent vive and Sulphur.

equivalences.with: mixture of Argent vive and Sulphur (volatile and fixed)
equivalences.quote: a mixture of Argent vive and Sulphur, that is to say, of the volatile and the fixed

quotes.text: the philosophers have two sorts of compounds

terms.meaning: The two components to be united. They act on each other and are reciprocally volatilized and fixed until perfectly fixed; Argent vive is the volatile, Sulphur the fixed.

equivalences.quote: Argent vive and Sulphur, that is to say, of the volatile and the fixed

quotes.text: make a perfect union of the volatile with the fixed

terms.meaning: Operations named as conditions: perfect dissolution follows proportioned digestion and putrefaction (end of the Second Key); extraction of the Fixed Salt needs convenient digestion and slow distillation.

quotes.text: not accomplished till after a convenient digestion and a slow distillation

variants: affusion of the water on the body
terms.meaning: Pouring the distilled water back onto the body, repeated many times, to impregnate the Mercury.

quotes.text: the affusion of the water on the body, reiterated many times, impregnates, fattens, and fertilizes our Mercury

terms.meaning: What animates the Water once the faeces are washed free of blackness; works all the wonders of the Art. The Balm of Life is said to be hidden in the faeces.

quotes.text: then your Water shall be animated with this Fiery Essence, which works all the wonders of our Art

terms.meaning: The operator. One who can sublime the Stone 'justly deserves the name of a philosopher'.

quotes.text: He who knows how to sublime the Stone philosophically, justly deserves the name of a philosopher

variants: the Serpent, born of the Slime of the earth
terms.meaning: Something to be purified in the first work; not further defined.

quotes.text: purify the Serpent, born of the Slime of the earth

sources.name: Eudoxus
sources.work: The Six Keys of Eudoxus, Opening Into the Most Secret Philosophy
sources.use: Named in the chapter heading as author of the Keys; the whole chunk is presented as his text.

sources.name: Hermes
sources.quote: In the caverns of the metals there is hidden the Stone
sources.use: Supports: cited repeatedly as authority. On the First Key (Stone hidden in the caverns of metals; 'What is born of the Crow is the beginning of this Art'); the Stone as 'vine of the Wise'; power 'not integral until it be turned into earth'; Water excites the fixed Nature; the first thing is the water issuing from the Stone, foundation of the Art; the water growing thicker and harder as a sign of success.

sources.name: Artefius
sources.use: Named with Trevisan and Flammel as among the 'sincerest' who still passed over the Preparation of Mercury in silence.

sources.name: Trevisan
sources.use: As Artefius: kept silence on the Preparation of Mercury.

sources.name: Flammel
sources.use: As Artefius: kept silence on the Preparation of Mercury.

sources.name: John Pontanus
sources.use: Supports: the Stone's superfluities become a true essence; to separate anything from the subject shows ignorance; the whole compound is perfected by 'our Fire'. Used against discarding the heavy part.

sources.name: Cosmopolite
sources.quote: All things must therefore being purged make Fire and Water to be Friends, which they will easily do in their earth, which had ascended with them.
sources.use: Supports: how to reconcile fire and water in their own earth.

sources.name: Senior
sources.quote: the highest fume should be reduced to the lowest
sources.use: Supports: precept for uniting volatile with fixed by bringing the vapour back onto the residue.

sources.name: Geber
sources.quote: a mixture of Argent vive and Sulphur
sources.use: Supports: definition of the compound of Art as volatile and fixed reciprocally fixed into perfect Fixity.

ambiguities.quote: Salt, Sulphur and Mercury --- which are the spirit, the soul, and the body
readings: A positional one-to-one mapping: Salt = spirit, Sulphur = soul, Mercury = body.
Only a collective equivalence: the three principles are the triad spirit/soul/body, with no pairing intended.
ambiguities.basis: The list order suggests reading A, but nothing else in the chunk confirms it, and elsewhere the Fixed Salt is extracted from the body/earth (IV.3 ¶7) and Mercury is what is being prepared (IV.3 ¶5, ¶7), which does not clearly fit Salt = spirit or Mercury = body.

ambiguities.quote: at which the operation of the Second Key of the First Work is ended
readings: The Keys are sub-stages within the Works: the First and Second Keys belong to the First Work.
'Works' and 'Keys' overlap differently: IV.3 ¶9 places impregnating the Mercury until 'fit to be fixed' at 'the end of the second Work', which seems to fall within the Third Key.
ambiguities.basis: IV.3 ¶3 speaks of 'the three works' as analogous and deliberately confused; IV.3 ¶5 'Second Key of the First Work'; IV.3 ¶9 'the end of the second Work' and 'not altogether the same in the Second as in the Third Work'.

ambiguities.quote: the distillation which is made by the rays of the Sun and Moon
readings: A literal use of sunlight and moonlight in the distillation.
A figurative expression for the Secret Fire's action, which no philosopher openly reveals.
ambiguities.basis: The same paragraph says the Secret Fire is never openly revealed and is 'this Nature wholly Divine'; nothing in the chunk decides between the readings.

ambiguities.quote: which contains in its veins the blood of the Pelican
readings: The same as the Fixed Salt, 'the Blood of our Stone' (IV.3 ¶7).
An unexplained image for some vital content of the white Stone.
ambiguities.basis: Both use 'blood' for something within the Stone, but the text never links them explicitly.

ambiguities.quote: it is the Sea of the Wise, in which they angle for their mysterious Fish
readings: The Fish is the seed or Sulphur extracted from the body in the First Key.
ambiguities.basis: IV.3 ¶3 says the First Key extracts the seed out of the body, but the Fish is never glossed.

ambiguities.quote: for it is Nature which makes it in a manner incomprehensible to the Artist
readings: In the First Key the Artist only assists Nature, which makes the compound.

This sits uneasily with IV.3 ¶3, where the First Key 'forms the Stone' and the Artist cuts off the Black Dragon's head in the first operation; perhaps Nature makes the compound and the Artist then purifies it.

threads.note: The chapter heading announces six Keys; only the First to Third appear in this chunk, so the Fourth to Sixth should follow.
The author promises to 'enlarge myself more than others have done on this Third Key'; the Third Key's treatment continues past the end of this chunk.
'the compound of Nature, whereof I have spoken in the First Key' refers back to IV.3 ¶3.
The chunk ends mid-thought with 'shines....', so the passage on the water's names continues in the next chunk.
'The compound of Art is not altogether the same in the Second as in the Third Work' anticipates a later treatment of the Third Work.
